content:
Full design record for T-007 — instant replay export/remux pipeline. Pairs with N-003 (capture), N-004 (encoder matrix), N-005 (rolling buffer). Binding for any later implementation ticket.

## 1. Responsibility scope (binding)

The export/remux pipeline is a helper-side module sitting between the rolling segment buffer (T-006) and the user's final MP4 file. It:

- Consumes a `ReplaySnapshot` returned by `replay.save(durationSeconds)` (T-006 §5).
- Turns the pinned fMP4 segments into a single playable MP4 file with `+faststart`.
- Does its own work on a separate Tokio task — never blocks capture, encode, or segment writing.
- Calls `replay.snapshot_release(snapshot_id)` exactly once when done (success, failure, or cancel).
- Owns final-file naming, temp-file safety, and atomic move into the user's destination dir.

It does NOT:

- Touch the rolling buffer's directory tree or any committed `.m4s` file (read-only).
- Re-trigger capture, force a new IDR, or change encoder configuration.
- Decide UI placement of progress, success, or failure notifications (T-008).
- Implement audio encode (separate ticket); only reserves the muxing slot.

## 2. Boundary with T-006

Single hand-off direction: T-006 → T-007. T-007 reads from the pinned snapshot via `init_segment_path` + each `SegmentRef.path`. The export task:

- Is started only after `replay.save(...)` returns. It is not allowed to call into the segment buffer mid-export except to call `replay.snapshot_release(snapshot_id)` on completion.
- Reads files via the page cache (sequential O_RDONLY). No locks acquired.
- Treats `SegmentRef.pts_start_90k` / `pts_end_90k` / `is_keyframe_first` / `discontinuity` / `sample_table` as ground truth — never re-parses to "second-guess" the buffer.
- Releases the snapshot exactly once. Guard pattern: `SnapshotGuard(Arc<Snapshot>)` whose `Drop` calls `snapshot_release` if it has not already fired.

## 3. Export state machine (binding)

States:

```
IDLE
 │ replay.save returns ReplaySnapshot
 ▼
QUEUED
 │ worker picks up
 ▼
PROBING              ── reason ─▶ FAILED
 │ inspect SPS/PPS/profile/level/timebase/IDR-front per SegmentRef
 ▼
PLANNING             ── reason ─▶ FAILED
 │ choose mode: fast | lead-reencode | discontinuity | full-reencode
 ▼
EXECUTING ┐
 │        ├── COPY            (fast path / non-discontinuity stretches)
 │        ├── REENCODE_HEAD   (lead trim mid-GOP)
 │        ├── REENCODE_BRIDGE (each discontinuity)
 │        └── REENCODE_FULL   (max-compat or fallback)
 ▼
MUXING               ── reason ─▶ FAILED
 │ assemble moov + mdat into temp file; +faststart guaranteed
 ▼
VALIDATING           ── reason ─▶ FAILED
 │ ffprobe sanity, container check, first-frame decode probe
 ▼
FINALIZING           ── reason ─▶ FAILED
 │ fsync temp, atomic rename to final, fsync parent dir, snapshot_release
 ▼
DONE

Any state → CANCELLING (on user cancel) → CANCELLED
Any state → FAILED on terminal error
DONE / FAILED / CANCELLED → IDLE (worker picks next queue item)
```

State transitions are explicit and event-emitting. The UI never has to infer the active stage from elapsed time. This is the structural answer to "the UI froze during save" — every state advances or emits `export.stalled` within a bounded window.

## 4. Operating modes (binding)

Mode is chosen exactly once in PLANNING and never changes mid-execution. If a mode's preconditions fail at execution time, the export FAILS — it does not silently fall back to a different mode (that hides cost from the user and is how v1.1.x produced silent re-encodes).

### 4.1 Fast path (`mode = fast`)

Stream-copy concat into MP4. Preconditions, ALL must hold:

- `segments[0].is_keyframe_first == true`.
- `trim_start_pts_90k == segments[0].pts_start_90k` (head trim already on IDR / segment boundary) OR head sample on an acceptable random-access point inside the head segment's sample table.
- `has_discontinuity == false`.
- All segments share: `codec`, `profile_idc`, `level_idc`, `timescale`, `width`, `height`, `pixel_format`, identical SPS, identical PPS.
- Encoded sample timing is contiguous: `segments[i].pts_end_90k == segments[i+1].pts_start_90k`.

Execution:

- Build a single MP4 `moov` from the concatenated sample tables (preserve sample durations exactly).
- Concatenate `mdat` payloads in segment order; no re-stamping, no re-fragmenting.
- Write moov BEFORE mdat (faststart). Use a two-pass mux: first pass computes sizes; second pass writes moov, then streams mdat.
- Trim tail by truncating sample table; the final sample's PTS ≤ `trim_end_pts_90k`.
- Output container: plain MP4 (`.mp4`), single H.264 video track, audio track slot reserved.

### 4.2 Lead trim re-encode (`mode = lead-reencode`)

Trim starts mid-GOP. Strategy: re-encode the head GOP only, copy the rest.

Preconditions:

- `has_discontinuity == false`.
- All segments compatible (same conditions as fast path except for head trim).
- The trim point falls inside `segments[0]`, after its first sample, before its last sample.

Execution:

1. Decode `segments[0]` from its IDR up to `trim_end_pts_90k_of_head_gop`.
2. Drop samples whose PTS < `trim_start_pts_90k`; keep the remainder.
3. Re-encode the kept samples with **libx264 only** (Linux rule: HW for live, CPU for re-encode, no exceptions — N-004 §13). Parameters match source: profile/level/colour primaries/transfer/matrix/range/timebase. CRF target 18, preset `veryfast`. Output ends with a fresh IDR so the next (copied) segment concatenates cleanly.
4. Concat re-encoded head GOP + `segments[1..]` stream-copied.
5. Mux as in §4.1.

Output codec: H.264 baseline-compatible with source profile; never AV1; never HEVC if source was H.264.

### 4.3 Discontinuity re-encode (`mode = discontinuity`)

Snapshot spans a `formatChanged` or other discontinuity event. Strategy: bracket each crossing with a re-encoded bridge; stream-copy compatible stretches outside the brackets.

Preconditions:

- `has_discontinuity == true`.
- `discontinuity_at_pts_90k` list is non-empty.

Execution:

1. For each crossing at PTS `Pc`, identify a **bridge interval** `[Pc - 1 GOP, Pc + 1 GOP]` rounded out to segment boundaries.
2. Decode bridge intervals from the surrounding segments; re-encode with libx264 to a single common output profile (the higher of the two if they differ; or the user's chosen output profile under advanced settings).
3. Stream-copy segments wholly outside any bridge interval.
4. Concat: copy → bridge → copy → bridge → copy ... in PTS order.
5. Mux as in §4.1.

Escape valve: if bridges collectively exceed 60 % of total snapshot duration, escalate to `mode = full-reencode` BEFORE execution starts (the cost case where bridging beats full re-encode evaporates). Escalation happens in PLANNING; once EXECUTING begins the mode is locked.

### 4.4 Maximum compatibility full re-encode (`mode = full-reencode`)

User toggle "Maximum compatibility" forces a single-pass libx264 re-encode of the entire snapshot. Also used as the escape valve from §4.3 and as the safety net when probe results are inconsistent in a way the matrix in §4.5 does not cover.

Execution:

1. Decode all segments in PTS order (segments are fMP4 fragments — ffmpeg handles seamless concat decode).
2. Re-encode with libx264; preset `medium`; CRF 20; keyframe interval 2 s.
3. Mux as in §4.1.

This mode is the v1.1.0 replay finalization safety net expressed as policy: when in doubt, libx264 the whole thing on the CPU. Linux NEVER asks the hardware encoder to re-encode (N-004 §13).

## 5. Probe / planning matrix (binding)

PLANNING decides mode using these rules in order. First match wins:

1. User has set "Maximum compatibility" toggle on this export → `full-reencode`.
2. `has_discontinuity == true`:
   - Bridges < 60 % of snapshot → `discontinuity`.
   - Else → `full-reencode`.
3. Any pairwise mismatch in {codec, profile_idc, level_idc, timescale, width, height, pixel_format, SPS, PPS} across `segments[*]` → `full-reencode`.
4. Trim is mid-GOP at the leading edge → `lead-reencode`.
5. Otherwise → `fast`.

PLANNING produces a `PlanReport { mode, copy_ranges, reencode_ranges, est_output_bytes, est_duration_s, expected_fps }` that is included in the `export.started` event. The UI never has to guess what is about to happen.

## 6. Cadence / FPS preservation (binding)

Carries forward the v1.1.0 replay FPS / cadence detection work. The pipeline NEVER synthesises a fixed 60 fps cadence by duplicating frames.

- **Fast and lead-reencode:** sample timing is preserved exactly. The MP4 sample table carries the original per-sample `sample_delta` values from the fragments. No re-stamping. Observed cadence = `(trim_end_pts_90k − trim_start_pts_90k) / sample_count`.
- **Discontinuity and full-reencode:** the decoder feeds real PTS deltas into the encoder. libx264 receives `-vsync passthrough`-equivalent (no implicit CFR coercion). Output retains the source cadence — including jitter, dropped frames, and any actual variance the encoder layer emitted.
- The PlanReport's `expected_fps` is the observed cadence, not a rounded marketing number.
- `export.completed.fps_observed` is the actually-mux'd cadence. UI displays it next to the file path. Any divergence > 5 % from `expected_fps` triggers a diagnostics dump.
- `samples_duplicated_total` MUST always be zero in production. Any non-zero value is a defect and triggers a `diagnostics-dump` event; the export still succeeds but is logged.

## 7. Audio sidecar muxing slot (binding, future-proofing only)

The `ReplaySnapshot` shape in T-006 will be extended (separate audio ticket) with:

```
audio_segments: Option<Vec<AudioSegmentRef>>,
audio_codec: Option<AudioCodec>,
audio_timescale: Option<u32>,
audio_sample_rate: Option<u32>,
audio_channels: Option<u16>,
audio_trim_start_pts: Option<i64>,
audio_trim_end_pts: Option<i64>,
```

T-007's mux step has an `if let Some(audio) = snapshot.audio_segments { ... }` slot:

- Audio sidecar = AAC-LC, single track, shared `t0_ns` with video (v1.1.0 audio sidecar stability fix is preserved by keeping a single time origin).
- Audio is ALWAYS stream-copied in v2.0.0 — even when video is re-encoded — because the audio buffer is its own segmented track with IDR-like access at every 1024-sample frame (~21 ms).
- Audio trim is sample-accurate at `audio_trim_start_pts` (mapped from `trim_start_pts_90k`); priming samples are trimmed via `edts/elst` edit list, not by re-encoding the head AAC frame (that is the v1.1.0 fix).
- If `audio_segments.is_none()`, the mux step produces video-only MP4; no behaviour change.

This slot exists so T-007 implementation does not need a redesign when audio lands.

## 8. Final file naming and temp file strategy (binding)

Output directory (configurable): default `$XDG_VIDEOS_DIR/Cove Replays/` on Linux, `%USERPROFILE%\Videos\Cove Replays\` on Windows. Created lazily; mode 0700 on Linux.

Final file name template: `Replay-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<HHMMSS>-<duration>s.mp4` in local time, with `-<n>` suffix if collision.

Temp file: `<output_dir>/.cove-replay-<snapshot_id>.partial.mp4`. Dot-prefix hides it from file managers and most indexers. Same filesystem as final → enables atomic rename.

If the user's chosen output dir is on a different filesystem than the helper's state dir, temp is still placed in the OUTPUT dir to keep rename atomic.

Orphan tracking: a JSONL `$XDG_STATE_HOME/cove-screen-recorder/exports/manifest.jsonl` records every `<temp_path, started_at, snapshot_id>` BEFORE the temp file is created and `<temp_path, ended_at, outcome>` when it finishes. On next helper launch, any temp not closed in the manifest is unlinked (best-effort) and its line marked `orphan-cleaned`.

## 9. Atomic final move (binding)

1. Write mux output to temp.
2. fsync(temp_fd).
3. close(temp_fd).
4. Compute SHA-256 of temp (single sequential read).
5. `rename(temp_path, final_path)` — POSIX atomic within the same filesystem; on Windows use `MoveFileExW(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH)`.
6. Open output-dir, fsync the directory fd (POSIX) / `FlushFileBuffers` on the directory handle if available (Windows; degrades to no-op on FAT-family).
7. Update exports manifest: line `outcome = success`.
8. Emit `export.completed` with final_path + bytes + sha256.

If any step fails: unlink temp (best-effort), update manifest `outcome = failed`, release snapshot, emit `export.failed`.

## 10. Snapshot release policy (binding)

The snapshot pin is released **exactly once** via `replay.snapshot_release(snapshot_id)`. The pin is held for the lifetime of the `SnapshotGuard` value owned by the export task.

Release happens in these scenarios:

| Outcome | When release fires | Where in code |
| ------- | ------------------ | ------------- |
| DONE    | After successful FINALIZING | explicit release before `export.completed` emit |
| FAILED  | On error from any state | guard's Drop |
| CANCELLED | After CANCELLING completes | guard's Drop |
| Helper crash mid-export | Process exit → pid.lock released → next launch's recovery reclaims orphan pins via T-006 recovery layers | implicit via OS process teardown |

The guard is `#[must_use]` and panics in debug builds if dropped without an outcome having been recorded. In release builds, drop releases the pin and logs `snapshot-released-on-drop` with the current state — this is a safety net, not the primary path.

## 11. Cancel semantics (binding)

User issues `export.cancel(export_id)`. The export task transitions to CANCELLING at the next sub-stage boundary:

- COPY: cancellation is checked between segments. Mid-segment copy completes (≤ 2 s of work).
- REENCODE_*: cancellation flushes the encoder, closes the ffmpeg process gracefully, releases the decoder. ffmpeg has up to 5 s to drain; otherwise it is SIGKILLed.
- MUXING: cancellation discards the in-progress moov/mdat write; temp file is unlinked.
- VALIDATING / FINALIZING: cancellation is REJECTED (treated as no-op). These stages are short (< 500 ms typically); allowing cancel here creates a race with the atomic rename. UI must keep the cancel button disabled past MUXING.

On successful cancel:
- Temp file unlinked.
- Snapshot released.
- `export.cancelled { export_id, stage, partial_bytes }` emitted.

There is no partial-file recovery option — cancel always discards. The user's mental model is "I cancelled it; it's gone."

## 12. Queue behaviour (binding)

The export pipeline runs a **single-worker FIFO queue**. Multiple saves in quick succession:

- Each `replay.save(...)` creates and pins its own `ReplaySnapshot` in T-006 immediately (within 250 ms + encoder fragment latency).
- All snapshots stack in the queue independently. T-006 holds them pinned; the rolling buffer keeps growing under the configured replay window. The user CAN keep saving while another export is running.
- The worker processes one export at a time. Concurrent ffmpeg processes on the same machine would steal CPU from the live encoder (libx264 is CPU-heavy) — single-worker is the design choice.
- Queue depth cap: 8. Past 8 outstanding exports, `replay.save(...)` still succeeds (it just produces a snapshot) but the export submission returns `export.rejected { reason: queue-full }` and the snapshot is released immediately. UI surfaces "Too many pending exports — please wait."
- Queue is in-memory only; helper crash loses queue state. Snapshots whose export had not yet started are recovered by T-006's session recovery flow and offered to the user as recoverable replays.

## 13. Anti-freeze invariants (binding — the v1.1.x lesson made structural)

The v1.1.x freeze-during-save bug cannot reoccur because:

1. **Snapshot is paths, not bytes** (T-006 §5). The export task receives only paths; no copy in the save call.
2. **Export runs on a dedicated Tokio task.** It never holds any lock that the capture or encoder tasks need. The only shared state with T-006 is `pinned_by[snapshot_id]`, a refcount touched once on save and once on release.
3. **The state machine is event-emitting.** Every transition emits an IPC event. The UI never has to infer state from elapsed time; it transitions when the event arrives.
4. **Watchdog timer.** A per-export watchdog fires `export.stalled { stage, last_progress_ms_ago }` if no progress event has been emitted for 5 s in COPY / 10 s in REENCODE_* / 2 s in MUXING / VALIDATING / FINALIZING. Stalled DOES NOT auto-kill; it surfaces the stall to the UI and the user decides.
5. **ffmpeg invocations are bounded.** ffmpeg child processes inherit a stdin pipe; the export task can issue `q\n` (graceful) and SIGKILL (hard) on cancel or timeout. ffmpeg is NEVER invoked in a "retry-on-error" loop (the v1.1.x bug). One try; structured error; surface to UI.
6. **Capture is not paused for the duration of any export stage.** Even REENCODE_FULL of a 10-minute snapshot does not stop the rolling buffer from accepting new fragments.

## 14. Failure modes (binding catalogue)

| Reason code | Stage where surfaced | Severity | Cleanup action |
| ----------- | -------------------- | -------- | -------------- |
| `snapshot-read-failed` | PROBING | fatal | release snapshot, unlink temp (none yet), emit failed |
| `probe-codec-mismatch-unrecoverable` | PROBING | fatal | escalates planning to `full-reencode`; not surfaced as failure |
| `probe-sps-pps-missing` | PROBING | fatal | release, emit failed (this means T-006 produced a malformed segment — file a bug) |
| `ffmpeg-spawn-failed` | EXECUTING | fatal | release, emit failed; reason includes errno / WinError |
| `ffmpeg-exited-nonzero` | EXECUTING | fatal | release, unlink temp, emit failed; reason includes stderr tail (last 8 KB) |
| `reencode-libx264-missing` | EXECUTING | fatal | release, emit failed; dev hint: rebuild with libx264 |
| `mux-faststart-failed` | MUXING | fatal | release, unlink temp, emit failed |
| `validate-ffprobe-failed` | VALIDATING | fatal | release, unlink temp, emit failed; do NOT promote a broken file |
| `validate-first-frame-decode-failed` | VALIDATING | fatal | as above |
| `finalize-rename-failed` | FINALIZING | fatal | release, unlink temp, emit failed; dev hint: cross-filesystem |
| `finalize-disk-full` | FINALIZING | fatal | release, unlink temp, emit failed |
| `cancel-requested` | any | controlled | release, unlink temp, emit cancelled |
| `helper-shutdown` | any | controlled | release (via guard Drop on process exit), temp left as orphan for next-launch cleanup |

Each fatal failure dumps the last 30 s of T-007 diagnostics counters (§16) plus the export's PlanReport into `$XDG_STATE_HOME/cove-screen-recorder/diagnostics/<export_id>.json`. Same shape as N-003 / N-004 / N-005 diagnostics — same triage tool works.

## 15. Helper exit mid-export (binding)

If the helper exits (graceful shutdown OR crash) while EXECUTING / MUXING / VALIDATING / FINALIZING:

- The export task is dropped. The `SnapshotGuard` Drop releases the pin to T-006.
- The temp file is NOT deleted by the dying process (cannot rely on shutdown handlers running).
- The exports manifest still has the `started` entry without an `ended` entry.
- On next launch, the helper:
  1. Reads `$XDG_STATE_HOME/cove-screen-recorder/exports/manifest.jsonl`.
  2. For each entry without an `ended` line, unlinks the temp file (best-effort) and appends `outcome = orphan-cleaned`.
  3. If the original snapshot's session is recoverable (T-006's recovery layers find segments), it is offered to the user via `replay.recoverable_sessions()` so they CAN re-trigger the export with the same trim window.

The user never sees a half-written `.mp4` in their output dir.

## 16. Diagnostics counters (binding)

Emitted at 1 Hz during EXECUTING and on every state transition. Pairs with N-003 §14 / N-004 §16 / N-005 §16 so any delay can be triangulated to its source layer.

```
export_started_total
export_completed_total { mode }
export_failed_total { reason }
export_cancelled_total
export_queue_depth
export_queue_rejected_total

export_stage_duration_ms.{queued, probing, planning, copy, reencode_head, reencode_bridge, reencode_full, muxing, validating, finalizing} { p50, p95, p99 }

bytes_in_total              # total bytes read from pinned segments
bytes_out_total             # bytes written to temp before rename
bytes_copied_total          # subset of bytes_out_total that was stream-copied
bytes_reencoded_in_total    # bytes fed to the libx264 input
bytes_reencoded_out_total   # bytes produced by libx264

samples_total               # total video samples in the snapshot
samples_copied_total
samples_reencoded_total
samples_duplicated_total    # MUST be 0; any non-zero is a bug
samples_dropped_total       # MUST be 0 outside of leading/trailing trim

reencode_seconds_total
reencode_pixels_total
reencode_libx264_kfps       { p50, p95 }

fps_observed_in
fps_observed_out
fps_divergence_pct          # |out - in| / in × 100; > 5 % triggers dump

ffmpeg_spawn_latency_ms     { p50, p95, p99 }
ffmpeg_exit_code_last

final_file_move_latency_ms  { p50, p95, p99 }
final_file_size_bytes
final_file_sha256_compute_latency_ms

temp_file_orphan_cleaned_total
exports_manifest_append_latency_ms { p50, p95 }
```

`fps_observed_out` is computed from the muxed sample table, not from ffmpeg's stderr. That is the v1.1.0 cadence-detection fix made structural.

## 17. Progress / cancel / error event surface (binding)

All events flow on the existing helper → Electron IPC bus (T-004 shape). Strict envelope: `{ kind, export_id, ts_ns, payload }`.

```
export.queued      { export_id, snapshot_id, requested_duration_s }
export.started     { export_id, mode, plan: PlanReport, est_duration_s, est_output_bytes }
export.progress    { export_id, stage, pct, bytes_in, bytes_out, samples_processed, samples_total, eta_ms }
export.stalled     { export_id, stage, last_progress_ms_ago }
export.completed   { export_id, final_path, bytes, sha256, duration_s, mode, fps_observed_out }
export.failed      { export_id, stage, reason_code, details, diagnostics_path }
export.cancelled   { export_id, stage, partial_bytes }
export.rejected    { export_id, reason: "queue-full" }
```

UI invariants this surface gives T-008:

- `export.started` arrives within ≤ 500 ms of save click in the fast-path common case.
- `export.progress` arrives at ≥ 1 Hz from EXECUTING onward.
- Either `export.completed` or `export.failed` or `export.cancelled` is the terminal event — exactly one per export_id.
- The UI's spinner is bound to the existence of an active `export_id`, NOT to a timer. The freeze bug cannot reoccur because the spinner ends when the terminal event arrives.

## 18. Validation matrix (binding — what the implementer must verify)

Fast path:
- 1080p60 / 1440p60 / 4K60 at 12 / 25 / 50 Mbps, NVENC source → trim-on-IDR concat.
- Same matrix with VAAPI source.
- Same matrix with QSV source (Linux Arc, Windows).
- Same matrix with libx264 source.

Lead trim re-encode:
- Mid-GOP trim at 30 s / 60 s / 2 m / 5 m / 10 m on all four backends.
- Verify the re-encoded head GOP ends with an IDR (sample table inspection).

Discontinuity:
- Force `formatChanged` mid-session (resize the source window). Save snapshot spanning the change. Verify bridge contains one full IDR-to-IDR re-encoded segment.
- Snapshot with two discontinuities < 60 % of total → `discontinuity` mode used.
- Snapshot with discontinuities > 60 % → escalated to `full-reencode`.

Maximum compatibility:
- Toggle on; verify full libx264 re-encode regardless of source.
- Linux: confirm HW encoder is NEVER touched in this path.

Cancel:
- Cancel during COPY: temp unlinked, snapshot released, event emitted within 2 s.
- Cancel during REENCODE_*: ffmpeg drains gracefully within 5 s; SIGKILLed at 5 s.
- Cancel during MUXING: temp unlinked.
- Cancel during VALIDATING / FINALIZING: rejected (UI disables button).

Crash recovery:
- SIGKILL helper during EXECUTING: next launch cleans orphan temp; snapshot is offered as recoverable via T-006 recovery layers.
- Same during MUXING / VALIDATING / FINALIZING: same.

Cadence:
- Capture jittery source (60 fps target, 50 fps actual). Export. Verify `fps_observed_out` ≈ 50, sample timing carries real per-frame deltas, `samples_duplicated_total == 0`.
- Verify with stream-copy AND with full re-encode.

Player compatibility (one save per mode):
- VLC, mpv, ffprobe (no warnings), Chrome `<video>`, Windows Media Player, QuickTime.

Multi-save:
- 4 saves issued in 2 s. All 4 snapshots pinned, all 4 exports complete serially, capture rate unchanged.
- Queue at depth 9: ninth export rejected with `export.rejected(queue-full)`.

Disk:
- Save during near-disk-full on output dir → `finalize-disk-full`, temp cleaned, snapshot released.
- Save during near-disk-full on state dir → T-006 raises `segment-sink-disk-full(pinned_by_save)`; the in-flight save completes (T-006 §7); subsequent saves rejected at the capture layer.

## 19. T-008 consumption contract

T-008 (UI ↔ engine integration) receives this event surface (§17) and these methods on the helper:

```
replay.save(durationSeconds)           -> ReplaySnapshot
replay.export_start(snapshot, options) -> export_id
replay.export_cancel(export_id)        -> void
replay.snapshot_release(snapshot_id)   -> void
```

`options` carries:

```
ExportOptions {
  output_path: Option<PathBuf>,         // None = default dir + auto name
  max_compat: bool,                      // forces full-reencode
  audio_mode: AudioMode,                 // default | mute | passthrough (audio ticket)
}
```

Electron renderer NEVER sees frames, NEVER sees segment paths, NEVER touches ffmpeg directly. It receives `export.*` events and renders progress + the final `final_path`.

## 20. Out of scope (deferred — explicitly recorded)

- Audio encode itself (slot reserved in §7; separate ticket).
- HDR tone-mapping policy on export (P010 source + SDR output). Reuses N-004 deferral.
- AV1 export (encoder side deferred in N-004).
- User-facing trim adjustment UI (T-008).
- Cloud upload / share-link generation. Outside helper entirely.
- Multi-track exports (e.g., separate mic / system audio). Reuses N-003 multi-stream deferral.
- Subtitle / overlay burning.
- Per-export bitrate override (re-encode uses fixed CRF).
- GIF / WebM / image-sequence export. v2.0.0 outputs MP4 only.
- Codex review of the design itself (planning-only session; no source files changed).

## 21. Open implementation items (non-blocking for design freeze)

- ffmpeg-as-library vs ffmpeg-CLI subprocess: subprocess by default (process isolation; easy SIGKILL; matches v1.1.0 model). Library option deferred.
- libx264 thread count for re-encode: default to `min(num_cores − 2, 8)` to leave headroom for the live encoder. Tunable via advanced settings.
- Windows long-path support on output dir (`\\?\` prefix). Default on; tunable.
- Default output dir creation prompt vs silent. Tentatively silent on first export; user sees the path in `export.completed`.
- SHA-256 compute can be folded into the mux pass via a sink wrapper rather than a second read — micro-optimisation deferred.
- Exports manifest fsync policy: fsync on each append vs batched per minute. Default fsync per append; tunable.

These are notes for the implementation ticket. None of them block T-007's design freeze.
title: Instant replay export/remux pipeline design (T-007)
